result.title: Sweep Less, Steer More: Using Activation Steering Geometry for Reduced Hyperparameter Search
result.summary: Representation steering methods like difference-in-means (DIM) offer a lightweight approach to controlling LLM behavior, but their effectiveness varies widely across concepts, datasets, and layers, making principled deployment costly without exhaustive hyperparameter sweeps. We build on the discriminability index $d'$, a compute-cheap geometric measure of how well contrastive training activations separate along the steering direction. Across five behaviors on 3 models, we demonstrate uses beyond its established role as a dataset-level steerability predictor. First, in the multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) setting, we show that $d'$ reliably identifies performant layers at which to steer, eliminating the need for a layer-wise sweep. Second, we extend this analysis to open-ended multi-token generation, and find that $d'$ remains successful for layer selection across different settings. Lastly, we test whether the position of a generated token's representation on the DIM line predicts steering success on that individual example. In the MCQA setting, this works for high-$d'$ datasets but is inconsistent across behaviors, models, and training-token choices in open-ended generation. This highlights that methods developed and conclusions drawn in single-token MCQA settings do not necessarily transfer to open-ended generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究用对比激活沿 steering 方向的可分性指数 d′ 这一廉价几何度量，替代逐层超参数扫描；在 3 个模型的 5 种行为上表明 d′ 可选出有效 steer 层，但单个 token 位置预测 steering 成败仅在 MCQA 高 d′ 数据上成立。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本激活操作，但 d′ 这类廉价可分性统计可供核查能否用于挑选 LVR 中信噪较高的层与 token 位置，其“单 token 结论不迁移到多 token 生成”的负结果也与 latent 相似度的深度、位置效应相关。
